Symptomatic polycythemia can be treated by cautious phlebotomy to lower Hct to 55 to 65% plus simultaneous volume replacement with normal saline.
However, compensated and asymptomatic polycythemia does not require phlebotomy, regardless of Hct; phlebotomy eventually leads to iron deficiency and does not change the natural history.
Hyperuricemia can be treated with allopurinol 300 mg po once/day.
Anticoagulation therapy with warfarin is potentially harmful and its use should be individualized, but aspirin 81 mg po once/day is indicated to prevent thrombotic complications.
